title: Work IQ: Context IQ adds agents, skills and content sources to the prompt menu
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned Context IQ expansion from existing menu behaviour and general agent controls. The roadmap dates, licensing rules, blocking path and preview Graph operation are supported; expansion-specific defaults, controls and charges remain explicitly unconfirmed.

claims.claim: The support article's user-level Work IQ control is a button at the top right of the chat page.
claims.quote:

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview says actions are user scoped and access only what that user may see or do.

claims.quote: Every tool invocation is logged and evaluated, enabling auditability, usage analytics, rate limiting, and real-time compliance enforcement across agents and data sources.

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview does not establish that its user-scoping description covers the expanded Context IQ selection mechanism.
claims.quote: Searched: "Context IQ" licensing price credits identity actions Work IQ; read Work IQ overview and the Context IQ support article. Neither describes the expanded agent/skill selection mechanism or places it within the Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document whether agent or skill selection in the expansion uses the Work IQ invocation-logging path.

claims.quote: Searched: Context IQ expanded menu agent skill selection rollout default policy identity; "Context IQ" licensing price credits identity actions Work IQ. Read Work IQ overview and Context IQ support; neither specifies an identity for agents selected this way.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether the expanded menu's selected agents or skills only read or can take actions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Context IQ" "agents" "skills"; "Context IQ" licensing price credits identity actions Work IQ. Read Work IQ overview and Context IQ support; general action capabilities do not describe the planned menu's runtime behaviour.

claims.claim: The blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.
In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: Blocking is a general tenant-wide agent access control available for agents selected from the inventory.
claims.quote:
Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.
